clue.text: Constituent parts of cattle-food

parts.note: the ordinary voters of a constituency, read literally as the underground parts of the pasture cows eat

explanation.surface: A feed analysis listing what goes into cattle fodder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constituent' looks like a plain adjective, but it means a member of a constituency, so the phrase also means the rank-and-file voters a politician depends on.
explanation.definitionFit: The rank and file of a party, the ordinary voters, are its grass roots; pasture plants are what cattle graze.

clue.text: It's not only a harp that's. played with pluck

definitions.text: It's not only a harp that's. played with pluck

parts.words: It's not only a harp that's. played with pluck
parts.note: a harp is plucked, but a sport too is played with pluck, meaning courage

explanation.surface: Harps are not the only instruments one plucks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pluck' is the harpist's action and also courage, which any match is played with; the answer is also an adjective for plucky.
explanation.definitionFit: A sporting contest is played with courage, and the word also means brave as an adjective.

clue.text: Eager to make a sixpence once

parts.note: in pre-decimal British money sixpence was written 6d, i.e. VI (Roman six) and D for pence

explanation.surface: Someone keen to earn a sixpence in the old days.
explanation.walkthrough: Before 1971 British pennies were abbreviated d, so sixpence was 6d, here VI D.
explanation.definitionFit: Being avid is being keen, eager.

clue.text: Devices to create an outstanding image

definitions.text: Devices to create an outstanding image

parts.words: Devices to create an outstanding image
parts.note: 'outstanding' is read as standing out, a picture that seems three-dimensional

explanation.surface: Gadgets to project a brilliant public image.
explanation.definitionFit: These viewers present paired photographs so the picture appears in depth.

clue.text: It's different if Mum's lost her head

indicators.note: the mother's first letter, her head, is dropped

parts.note: Mum is mother

explanation.surface: Things are not the same now that Mum has panicked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost her head' seems to mean panicked, but it removes the first letter of MOTHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Other means different, not the same one.

clue.text: Edward took in an aircraft worker and set off

indicators.note: Ted holds the worker inside him

parts.note: Ted is a short form of Edward
a rigger assembles and adjusts an aircraft's rigging

explanation.surface: Edward gave a plane mechanic lodging and then left.
explanation.definitionFit: To trigger something is to set it off, start it.

clue.text: Goes out tidily ?

parts.note: 'tidily' is read as 'tide-ly', in the way of a tide, so this is water retreating down the shore

explanation.surface: Someone leaves the house neatly turned out.
explanation.definitionFit: When the tide falls back it recedes; the verb for that retreat of the sea is the one wanted.

clue.text: Frenchman serves up high-class grub, and in novel form

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' turns the food word bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written, a word for food
U is the old label for upper-class usage

indicators.note: the letters of the two little words take a new shape

explanation.surface: A Frenchman dishes up posh food in an unusual way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serves up' turns GRUB into BURG; 'novel form' rearranges AND IN to NDIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Burgundy, a French region, is a Frenchman.

clue.text: Three-dimensional unity can be strikingly shown

definitions.text: Three-dimensional unity can be strikingly shown

parts.words: Three-dimensional unity can be strikingly shown
parts.note: the word splits as solid plus a sense of oneness, and workers on strike show it

explanation.surface: A sculptural harmony can be displayed to dramatic effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strikingly' means by going on strike: workers show unity by walking out together.
explanation.definitionFit: Union members display mutual support and fellowship by striking together.

clue.text: The spinster locks the plant

parts.note: an unmarried woman is an old maid, a maiden
locks are tresses, i.e. hair

explanation.surface: An unmarried woman's tresses are compared with the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Maidenhair is a delicate fern, so a plant.

clue.text: Mouthed "Viva !"

definitions.meaning: a viva voce is a spoken examination at a university

explanation.surface: Someone silently forms the word 'Viva!' with their lips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Viva' looks like a cheer, but here it is the British university term for a spoken exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mouthed is spoken, and a viva is a spoken examination, both senses of the adjective.

clue.text: They're naturally inexperienced at selling tea, sugar, etc

definitions.text: They're naturally inexperienced at selling tea, sugar, etc

parts.words: They're naturally inexperienced at selling tea, sugar, etc
parts.note: 'inexperienced' gives green and sellers of dry goods give grocers, though the trade is in fruit and vegetables

explanation.surface: Shopkeepers new to selling groceries.
explanation.walkthrough: The trade sells green produce, so they are 'naturally' green; 'selling tea, sugar' describes grocers.
explanation.definitionFit: Shopkeepers selling fresh fruit and vegetables are named for green produce and the grocer's trade.

clue.text: Fair revolutionary happy to meet the requirement

parts.note: merry means cheerful, happy
there is enough to go round when the supply meets everyone's need

explanation.surface: A cheerful radical at a fair is pleased to fulfil the conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair revolutionary' suggests a just rebel, but it is a ride at a funfair that revolves.
explanation.definitionFit: A carousel at a funfair turns round and round, so it is a revolving attraction.

clue.text: Claims chop and change to be complete

indicators.note: 'chop and change' means keep altering, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Insurance claims are endlessly revised until finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges the ten letters of CLAIMS and CHOP; 'and' joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: To accomplish a task is to complete it.

clue.text: Stays around a party? That's how to get them tight

definitions.text: Stays around a party? That's how to get them tight

parts.words: Stays around a party? That's how to get them tight
parts.note: stays are a corset, which is tightened by threading cords through, not guests lingering and getting drunk

explanation.surface: Guests who linger at a party end up drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stays' are corsets and 'tight' means firmly drawn, not drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Threading cords through eyelets is the act of lacing up, which pulls a corset tight.

clue.text: Sticky sweet not too popular with EEC

definitions.text: Sticky sweet not too popular with EEC

parts.words: Sticky sweet not too popular with EEC
parts.note: a sweetener grown in Commonwealth colonies, less favoured by the European Economic Community, which grew beet instead

explanation.surface: A gooey confection that the European Community does not care for.
explanation.walkthrough: The EEC, forerunner of the European Union, protected its own sugar-beet farmers, so the tropical crop met tariffs.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar refined from a tall tropical grass is the sweetener the European beet growers competed against.

clue.text: Dog at last had puppies. That was splendid!

indicators.note: the final letter of the word dog is taken

parts.note: a dog that gives birth has littered

explanation.surface: Finally the dog had her pups, and it was wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that glittered sparkled brilliantly, looking splendid.

clue.text: Duck down

parts.note: 'Duck' looks like a command to crouch, but is the sea-bird whose soft breast feathers fill quilts

explanation.surface: A warning to lower one's head quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: This sea-duck gives its name to the soft feathers in an eiderdown quilt.

clue.text: Part of NZ quotation in round figures

indicators.note: the quotation sits inside the pair of round figures

parts.note: two noughts, each a round figure O
a tag is a short familiar quotation

explanation.surface: A New Zealand quote is given in round numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Otago is a region of New Zealand's South Island.

clue.text: About archaeological work local worker is angry

indicators.note: the local, a pub, goes around the excavation, so 'About' signals a container

parts.note: a local is a neighbourhood pub, an inn
an archaeological excavation is a dig
the worker ant is crossword shorthand for a worker

explanation.surface: Someone working on a local excavation is cross about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local worker' reads as one person, but splits: 'local' is the pub (INN) and 'worker' the ant.
explanation.definitionFit: Being indignant means feeling angry at something unfair.

clue.text: Gift for a former deb ?

parts.note: a present, and also the formal introduction at court that a debutante underwent in the past

explanation.surface: Choosing a present for a woman who came out in society years ago.
explanation.walkthrough: Debutantes were once formally presented to the monarch at court, a custom that ended in 1958.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift is a present made formally, and a debutante's introduction at court was her coming before the Queen.

clue.text: He perseveres at Treves

definitions.meaning: Trèves is the French name of a German city on the Moselle

explanation.surface: A man keeps going in a German city.
explanation.definitionFit: One who keeps trying is a persistent sort, and the German city on the Moselle has this name.

clue.text: It can be picked acrimoniously in Algeria

definitions.meaning: one picks a ... with someone in a quarrel
a city of colonial French Algeria, the port now called Annaba, had this name

explanation.surface: Something argued over in Algeria.
explanation.walkthrough: Bône was the French colonial name of Annaba, so the word for a quarrel's subject is also a place in Algeria.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a skeletal piece to pick is a grievance, and Bône was a port city of colonial Algeria.

clue.text: Adversity's are sweet

parts.note: Shakespeare's line in As You Like It, 'Sweet are the ... of adversity'

explanation.surface: Hard times bring their own sweetness.
explanation.walkthrough: The Duke in As You Like It says 'Sweet are the uses of adversity'; the clue fills that gap.
explanation.definitionFit: The quotation means hardship has its benefits or purposes.

clue.text: Cold comfort from unjust! magistrates

indicators.note: read as 'un-just', the word just removed from the magistrates

parts.note: justices of the peace are magistrates

explanation.surface: Unfair magistrates offer little consolation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unjust' is split as un + just: take JUST away from JUSTICES and what is left are frozen desserts, comfort on a hot day.
explanation.definitionFit: Frozen desserts are cold treats, hence a cold comfort.

clue.text: Bearing arms for family reasons

parts.note: entitled to display a heraldic coat of arms through one's lineage, not carrying weapons

explanation.surface: Someone carries weapons to defend their relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearing arms' looks military, but in heraldry a family bears arms on its shield.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes a person entitled to heraldic arms, usually inherited through the family.

clue.text: Loathe articles in disorder

indicators.note: the letters of the articles are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: the indefinite article is a
the definite article is the

explanation.surface: Someone detests things lying in a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' gives both A and THE; 'in disorder' rearranges those four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe is to detest strongly.

clue.text: They're intended to get the message

definitions.text: They're intended to get the message

parts.words: They're intended to get the message
parts.note: the people a letter is sent to, not those who understand a hint

explanation.surface: Some people are meant to understand what is being hinted at.
explanation.definitionFit: The people whose names are on letters are their recipients.
